reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every natural J>=2 and every real h>0, index nodes by Fin(J)={0,...,J-1} and define
  t_i=(h/2)(1-cos((i/(J-1))pi)),
  ell_j(X)=product_{k in Fin(J),k!=j} ((t_j-t_k)^(-1))(X-t_k),
  Lambda=sup_{s in [0,h]} sum_{j in Fin(J)} |ell_j(s)|.
The quotient in the node definition uses real coercions, so its denominator is the real number J-1. The ell_j are real Lagrange basis polynomials evaluated at real arguments, and Lambda is the real supremum of the indicated interval image. Then
  sum_{j in Fin(J)} |integral_0^h ell_j(s) ds| <= h Lambda.
The integrals use real Lebesgue measure with oriented endpoints; h>0 makes the interval order increasing. The absolute value is applied separately to each integral, followed by a finite sum. This theorem asserts precisely this total absolute integrated-weight bound, without adding signed normalization, individual positivity, an upper growth bound on Lambda, or quadrature exactness conclusions.
objects: J actual cosine nodes t_i on a real interval, real Lagrange basis polynomials ell_j, their interval absolute-sum supremum Lambda and the signed integrals of each basis polynomial whose individual absolute values are summed.
domains: J in N with J>=2; h in R with h>0; i,j,k in Fin(J). t:Fin(J)->R; ell:Fin(J)->R[X]; Lambda in R. Integration is over real s from 0 to h against Lebesgue measure. Every displayed sum/product ranges over the full finite index set subject to the indicated k!=j exclusion.
quantifiers: For every J>=2 and every h>0, the t,ell,Lambda are fixed by the displayed definitions and the single integrated-weight inequality holds. No existential coefficient or per-node positivity statement occurs. The supremum ranges over all real s in [0,h].
assumptions: J>=2 and h>0. Nodes,Lagrange polynomials and Lambda have the exact displayed definitions. The local parameter name _hJ does not remove J>=2 from the mathematical assumptions. No smoothness, probability law, weight sign or quadrature hypothesis is added.
conclusion: The sum of the absolute values of the signed basis integrals is at most h times Lambda: sum_j |integral_0^h ell_j(s)ds|<=h Lambda. This is the full explicit conclusion.
scopes: The absolute values are outside the individual integrals, not a single absolute value around a total sum. Lambda measures the pointwise sum of absolute basis values over [0,h]. The theorem does not separately assert signed total weight h, individual weight positivity, partition of unity, node injectivity or growth of Lambda. No material ambiguity is present.
constant_dependencies: The exact multiplicative bound is h Lambda, with Lambda defined from the J,h-dependent Lagrange basis and closed interval. No universal upper bound on Lambda or unspecified constant appears.
